artifacts.summary: Rules the lint is wired as a new trailing verify-deploy.sh gate 23 (not inserted beside gate 17), because 131+ existing by-number citations of gates 18-22 (especially gate 20) would be silently invalidated by any renumbering; enumerates the exact line-level change list in verify-deploy.sh, test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh, and the git-staging-scope.md bullet this task owns; confirms live 0-violation/14-passed lint state and blocking tier as safe; confirms no collision with task 304's RULE 3 addition to the sibling lint.

memory_candidates.content: When wiring a new numbered gate into verify-deploy.sh, prefer appending as a trailing gate over inserting beside a related sibling gate. Existing gates are cited by number across many test files and docs (observed: gate 20 alone had 131 by-number citations in this repo), so an insertion that renumbers subsequent gates silently invalidates all of them. A grep sweep for '[Gg]ate N\b' across *.md/*.sh/*.json for each candidate insertion point's downstream gate numbers is a cheap, decisive way to settle a placement question like this.

A lint already wired as a verify-deploy.sh gate can grow new detection rules (e.g. 'RULE 3') inside its own script without any gate-numbering or verify-deploy.sh change -- the gate block only cares about the script's exit code and --verbose [VIOLATION] output contract, not its internal rule count. Observed with lint-scoped-commit-boundary.sh (gate 17) gaining a RULE 3 in a sibling task with zero impact on gate wiring.
